title.narrative: More women, men, youth and vulnerable groups in Cambodia have access to safe and healthy working conditions

description.narrative: The CPO KHM227 addresses the critical need to strengthen Cambodia’s occupational safety and health (OSH) system, promoting safe and healthy working environments as a Fundamental Principle and Right at Work. Despite progress in regulatory development, both persistent and emerging risks—ranging from physical hazards to psychosocial stressors—continue to affect workers across sectors, particularly in high-risk industries such as the entertainment sector. During the biennium, the CPO supports the finalization and adoption of the National OSH Policy and the timely implementation of the 3rd National OSH Programme, with regular monitoring to ensure effective delivery. A key focus is enhancing workplace capacity in managing mental health and strengthening social dialogue and workplace cooperation. Target beneficiaries include workers, employers, and labour inspectors, particularly in sectors with high exposure to occupational risks. Special attention is given to improving equality and non-discrimination in the entertainment industry through continued capacity building on OSH, HIV/AIDS prevention, and substance abuse. In 2024, efforts included training labour inspectors and workplace committees, as well as engaging employers to raise awareness and improve compliance with national standards. These initiatives will continue in 2025, with a focus on building the technical capacity of labour officers to enforce OSH, HIV/AIDS, and drug prevention regulations more effectively. The strategy is implemented in close coordination with government bodies, notably the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training, and supported by international partners. Through these efforts, the CPO contributes to safer, more inclusive workplaces while reinforcing national commitments to decent work and health for all.
